x: Archibald (S.W.C.) was ordered to "fade out" and several others must have considered themselves lucky, for had there been more officials in the vicinity the number of contestants would have been considerably reduced at this point.

We travelled to Croydon on December 10th to meet our old rivals, Surrey W.C., over their West Wickham and back course, 9¾ miles to testing roads. Harold King took the lead from the start, closely followed by Archibald and Kemp, of the S.W.C., with Brown, A.
On only one occasion has this championship been won with a lower score, viz., in 1919, when the Surrey Walking Club, represented by Blackmore, Amer, Chilton and Archibald, scored 22 points only.
Eventually Richardson and Archibald were dropped in turn, and Pope, apparently increasing speed with each mile, finished over a hundred yards in front of Redman.
They, too, had their misfortunes in the disqualification of Archibald and the falling-back of Galloway, but superior reserve strength enabled them to survive.
